title: Four consoles, one runaway winner
lede: The Dreamcast opened the sixth generation of consoles and was the only one of the four to be cancelled inside three years. The other three makers are all still in the business. [3DO](/3do/) had left console hardware earlier, to become a game publisher.

blocks.title: Lifetime console sales, sixth generation
blocks.subtitle: Millions of units, each maker’s own figure.

items.label: Dreamcast (Sega)
items.note: To March 31, 2001, Sega’s count. Later totals of 9.13 to 10.6 million are unverified.[^2]

blocks.source: Sony Interactive Entertainment[^22], Microsoft[^24], Nintendo[^23] and Sega’s annual report 2001[^2]. The Sony and Microsoft figures are lower bounds. The Dreamcast figure excludes clearance sales after March 2001, so it understates the final total by an unknown amount.

blocks.title: Who won, who quit
blocks.subtitle: Each console’s lifetime sales and what became of its maker’s hardware business.

items.name: Dreamcast
items.text: Sega’s count to March 2001.[^2] Sega left hardware and became a publisher.

items.name: PlayStation 2
items.text: The best-selling of the four by a wide margin.[^22] It reached the United States on October 26, 2000.[^7]

items.name: GameCube
items.text: Released in Japan on September 14, 2001.[^23] Sega sold 1.22 million games for it in its first year as a publisher.[^3]

items.name: Xbox
items.text: Microsoft’s first console.[^24] Sega’s U.S. team expected Microsoft’s entry as early as September 2000.[^7]

blocks.source: As for the chart above. Sparklines: Dreamcast units by fiscal year in millions[^1][^2]; GameCube units by Nintendo fiscal year in ten-thousands[^23].

blocks.title: For every Dreamcast, about twenty PlayStation 2s
blocks.equation: 160 million ÷ 8.20 million = 19.5, rounded up to 20 icons. Each icon stands for one Dreamcast’s worth of PlayStation 2 sales.
blocks.source: Sony Interactive Entertainment[^22]; Sega annual report 2001[^2].

blocks.title: U.S. console market share, January to September 2000
blocks.subtitle: Share of the retail and mail-order channel before the PlayStation 2 arrived, according to PC Data.
blocks.source: PC Data figures as reported by the Register, October 9, 2000[^14]. In the weeks after the August price cut the Dreamcast’s share rose to just under 30%.
